headline: Lakefront Camping and Beach Access
reservation: Camping reservations must be made through the Nova Scotia Provincial Parks online system, typically opening in spring. Day-use access for the beach and picnic areas generally does not require a reservation, but check official status for seasonal gate closures.

days.title: Dollar Lake Waterfront

stops.name: Dollar Lake Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the large sandy beach area and supervised swimming during the peak summer months.

stops.name: Boat Launch and Cove
stops.detail: Explore the calm waters by canoe or kayak to see the forested shoreline of the Musquodoboit Valley.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes from Halifax; conditions vary on Route 357
days.note: The park is a popular local escape; weekday visits offer more seclusion.

days.title: Woodland Exploration

stops.name: Woodland Walking Trails
stops.detail: Hike through the mixed forest to observe local Nova Scotian flora and quiet interior lake views.

stops.name: Musquodoboit Valley Lookoffs
stops.detail: Drive a short distance outside the park to access elevated views of the winding river valley.

days.driving: Local driving within the park and surrounding valley roads
days.note: Black fly and mosquito activity is highest in June and early July.

days.title: Regional Backroads

stops.name: Musquodoboit Railway Trail
stops.detail: Visit this nearby rail-to-trail conversion for a flat walk or cycle through scenic wetlands.

stops.name: Gibraltar Rock
stops.detail: Take a short drive to this trailhead for a more challenging hike with views of the Musquodoboit River.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for regional exploration; check for road construction
days.note: Cellular service can be spotty in the deeper valley sections.

intel.title: Day-Use Lot
intel.text: The main parking area near the beach fills up on warm weekends and holidays. Arrive early or plan a mid-week visit to ensure a spot near the water.

intel.title: Variable Coverage
intel.text: Signal strength is reliable near the park entrance but may weaken significantly at the campsites and on the water. Do not rely on GPS for backroad navigation without offline maps.

intel.title: Rural Services
intel.text: The nearest fuel and full grocery services are located in Elmsdale or Musquodoboit Harbour. Ensure your tank is sufficient before heading into the interior valley roads.

intel.title: Park Operating Season
intel.text: The park typically operates for camping from June to October, while day-use gates may have different hours. Check the official park website for the exact seasonal opening dates.

intel.title: Trail Conditions
intel.text: Trails are mostly natural surface and can be muddy after rain. The beach area features boardwalks to improve access to the sand.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Halifax Stanfield (YHZ) and shop for supplies in Elmsdale before the 30-minute drive to the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the paved park roads; RV sites are available but check length restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The main beach facing west for sunset reflections over Dollar Lake.
